Boxoffy Weekend Recap · 2–4 October 2026

We Called ₹61 Crore. It Did ₹62.

And then we talked ourselves into ₹67 and got it wrong. Every number we published this weekend, graded against the actuals — the three that landed and the three that did not.
The Grade

Our pre-release call was better than our live one.

On Thursday night, before a single ticket was torn, we published ₹61 crore for Drishyam’s opening day. On Friday evening, with roughly two-thirds of the day’s shows already begun and ₹40.50 crore on the counter, we revised up to ₹67 crore and said the film was bigger than our model had allowed for.

The model was right. We were the problem.

Opening day, India netThu, pre-release₹61.00 Cr₹62.00 Cr−1.6%
Opening day, revisedafter 7.15pm FridayFri evening₹67.00 Cr₹62.00 Cr+8.1%
Saturday, India netSat 9pm₹50 Cr₹53.50 Cr−6.5%
Two-day totalSat 9pm₹117 Cr₹115.50 Cr+1.3%
North America, day oneFri 4.14pm CT$750K$800K−6.2%
Three-day weekendour published article callThu, pre-release₹185 Cr₹174–183 Cr+1% to +6%
North America weekendgraded MondaySat, from our scan$2.83–3.21Mopen—
The lesson, written down so we remember it. Both of our pre-release calls — ₹61 crore on the day and ₹185 crore on the weekend — landed inside a few per cent. Both of our intraday revisions moved away from the answer. We had more information on Friday evening than on Thursday night and we used it worse, because a number taken halfway through a day tells you about that half, and we read it as though it told us about the whole.

The Weekend

₹115.50 crore in two days, and a Saturday that held far better than we expected.

Friday was Gandhi Jayanti, a national holiday, which is why we and nearly everyone else braced for a steep Saturday. It did not come. The drop was 13.7%, not the quarter we had modelled.

DayIndia netOccupancyShowsFootfalls
Friday 2 OctGandhi Jayanti₹62.00 Cr60.1%15,75924,58,370
Saturday 3 Oct₹53.50 Cr48.1%16,86820,43,670
Sunday 4 Octour estimate₹58–67 Cr———
Three-day weekend₹174–183 Cr———

Exhibitors added 1,109 shows for Saturday over Friday. In the fifty cities we read ourselves they nudged Sunday up again, from 7,972 screenings to 8,034, after having under-booked it the night before. That is the trade voting with its own screens, and they only do it when a Friday sells.

The country is not watching this film evenly. On Saturday, Chennai ran 72.3% and Bengaluru 70.0% while Surat managed 13.7% and Ahmedabad 29.3%. For a Hindi thriller that is a strange map, and it is the same one we flagged before release: Gujarat was cold on this film in advance too, on more screenings than Maharashtra had.
Where It Ranks

Second biggest opening weekend of 2026, on a rule almost nobody applies.

Opening weekends get quoted loosely. Dhurandhar 2’s famous ₹339 crore “first three days” is Thursday to Saturday. Toxic’s ₹165.95 crore is Wednesday to Friday. Counted strictly Friday to Sunday, which is the only way these numbers compare, the 2026 board looks different.

North America

$800,000 on Friday, and the second biggest Indian opening weekend of the year.

Gitesh Pandya of Box Office Guru reported Drishyam’s Friday at $800,000, with Canada accounting for 37% of it — a far larger share than Canada’s 12.5% of the showtimes would suggest. Our own scan of 387 American cinemas on Saturday morning had the film running 37% ahead of Friday on tickets at the matched point of the day.

What we have actually measured, day by day

WeekendOur estimate———$2.83–3.21M

Read at the matched point of each day — Saturday 10.21am against Friday 11.33am, so Saturday had an hour less selling behind it, not more — the film was running 37% ahead on tickets and 18% ahead on both seats and showtimes. The shows closest to starting were furthest ahead: +13.2 points under four hours out, +9.3 points at four to eight.

We calibrate the dollar figure on Friday rather than on an assumed ticket price. Friday’s 11.33am read of 18,516 tickets became a reported $800,000, which is $43.21 of final gross per morning-counted ticket. That one factor absorbs walk-up, the cinemas outside the Fandango feed, and pricing — all the things an average-ticket-price assumption guesses at. Saturday’s 25,368 tickets through the same factor give $1.10 million, and the weekend follows from there.

A gap worth naming. Border 2, The Raja Saab, MSVP and Awarapan 2 have no reported North America gross at all. Four films worth over ₹1,300 crore worldwide between them, and the American box office record has nothing for any of them. The biggest Indian films in America are, in the official data, partly invisible.
How We Count

Where our numbers come from, and why they sometimes disagree with everyone else’s.

We do not take a figure from a press release and round it. For every major release we read the live seat maps on the booking systems the cinemas sell through — show by show, screen by screen, across fifty Indian cities and, for North America, 387 American and 48 Canadian cinemas. On the Thursday before this release that came to 6,36,693 seats counted across 7,448 shows in 667 cinemas.

Counting is only half of it. The number has to survive a check it could fail.

The check that matters. We counted the national chains two different ways on the same night. A hand scan at 9.44pm read 3,74,684 seats. The machine count, rolled back to that same minute, read 3,72,400 — 0.6% apart, from two methods that share no code and no operator. When two independent counts of the same thing agree that closely, the count is probably right. When they do not, we say so rather than publish the prettier one.

Three things we hold ourselves to, and they cost us this weekend as often as they helped. We label every estimate as an estimate. We publish the old number next to the new one whenever a call moves. And we grade every call against the actual, including the ones that miss — which is why three of the six lines in the table at the top of this page are against us.

A worked example from this weekend. On Friday night the trade figure for opening day was ₹66.75 crore from one tracker and ₹62.03 crore from another — a 7% gap between two credible sources. We said at the time that the lower one came from a narrower panel of cinemas. By Saturday night the higher source had revised down to ₹62.00 crore. The conservative number was the right one, and our own call sat above both.
First Weekend Review

Four out of five, and a career turn for Jaideep Ahlawat.

First half. Top notch, and the Jaideep Ahlawat and Ajay Devgn face-off is the absolute highlight of it. Dialogues that brought the audience to applause include “Aap humare 2 IG kha gaye” and “Madira peekar so gaye”. The dialogue-baazi is at the level of another Ajay Devgn film, Once Upon A Time In Mumbaai.

Ahlawat finally has a career turnaround film and this will change his trajectory. He is more menacing because he has a dirty energy about him, someone who can get rough with Vijay if it comes to that — where Akshaye Khanna was the more polished antagonist.

Second half. It nails what a Drishyam second half is for: twist, turn and plot detail. One piece did not fully convince — the reflection back on the second part felt a little convenient (no spoilers here). The background score carrying the story is always the main draw. The audience clapped through certain courtroom scenes.

This time the screenplay aura-farms both Ahlawat and Devgn in the second half, and some shots are built to make Devgn look good — worth paying attention to how the front-on framing lands and the side profile does not.

Verdict: 4 out of 5. A blockbuster plot-driven film where the audience is openly rooting for Vijay and his family, and it shows in the reactions in the hall. Shortcomings are a conversation for when it reaches OTT. For theatres, this is a big win.

Two films on the Netflix chart were in cinemas earlier this year. Vishwanath & Sons is in its third week in the Netflix top ten and also sits third on our North America theatrical board for the year at $1.63 million. Dhamaal 4 is in its fourth week on Netflix after a $507,000 American opening. A film can now sit in the American top ten for Indian releases and the Indian Netflix top ten inside the same quarter.

On Prime’s television side, Mirzapur sits eighth — the series, not the film, which took $1.00 million across its American opening weekend in September and is the fifth biggest Indian opening in North America this year.

Hype Index

Ramayana’s trailer has the highest engagement rate we have measured. Its view count does not match.

Ramayana: Part 1 opens internationally on 6 November and in India on 8 November, Diwali, on a reported ₹4,000 crore budget across both parts. With the release five weeks out, we re-ran the hype index against two films whose openings we now know.

FilmTrailer viewsLikesLike rateOpening day
Dhurandhar 2trailer 6 Mar9,24,23,62513,25,3281.434%₹102.55 Cr
Ramayana: Part 1trailer 29 Jul3,32,24,1755,38,8941.622%—
Drishyam: The Conclusiontrailer 14 Sep1,00,86,12861,2060.607%₹62.00 Cr

Ramayana’s like rate of 1.622% is the highest of the three — above Dhurandhar 2, which went on to post the biggest opening day in Hindi cinema. Drawn as a straight line through the two known points, that rate implies an opening day near ₹112 crore.

Why we are not calling ₹112 crore. Two points make a line, not a model. Dhurandhar 2’s 9.24 crore trailer views include six months of post-release traffic, which inflates a film that already succeeded and makes its like rate a dirty comparison. Ramayana’s is clean pre-release data. We will publish a number when we have advance booking to anchor it, not before.
The more interesting signal is that the music is outrunning the film. Jai Jai Ram has taken 5.7 crore views in a fortnight — about 40 lakh views a day — while the trailer is averaging 5 lakh a day across its life. For a devotional subject the music carries the film, and here it is carrying it eight times faster than the trailer is.
Grading

What we are on the hook for next.

North America is the one market where this report is published mid-event. The American weekend does not close until Sunday night Pacific, and the reported figures land on Monday, so every dollar number above is our own count rather than a studio’s. We would rather say that than wait a day and quietly publish the answer as if we had called it.

Sunday’s actual settles our ₹58–67 crore call and the ₹174–183 crore weekend. North America’s Sunday settles the $2.83–3.21 million estimate and whether Gitesh Pandya’s $2.5 million weekend call, which we think is conservative, holds. Both get graded here on 5 October, win or lose, next to the numbers above.
